issue.title: Fix date_histogram issues during a timezone DST switch

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The problem was in the difference between the two responses of the `preTz.getOffset` call. To solve this I only call it once.

The behaviour of `roundKey` changed that it is now returning the actual rounded timestamp rounded timestamp offsetted to UTC. The exact opposite is true for `valueForKey` which used to accept the UTC offsetted timestamp but now needs to work on the normal timestamp.

The tests for rounding are all passing, including the tests I added where the issue was shown.

Closes #8339

issue.title: Missing data in area chart

repository.name: kibana
repository.description: Your window into all of your data

issue.body:
_This is my very first day playing around with Kibana, pardon me if I'm missing the obvious._

I have a set of documents with a `created_at` date field that I want to draw as an area chart, and I was surprised by a "hole" in my data that looked like an anomaly:

![kibana_area_hole](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1564054/8625564/759b31b6-26f4-11e5-9744-78072bca4f69.png)

I zoomed in on this particular day to check if it was some artifact of the rendering scale, but there is indeed no data there:

![kibana_area_zoom](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1564054/8625579/856cf426-26f4-11e5-9b74-bcd1417e0dd3.png)

Double checking in the "Discover" tab, I can indeed see that 12 documents should be there, and even more surprising, I can see them on a bar chart with the exact same setup:

![kibana_bar_zoom](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1564054/8625589/990d30f4-26f4-11e5-86d9-2298cd6de2eb.png)

Using Kibana from [Docker official images](https://registry.hub.docker.com/_/kibana/):
- Version `4.1.1`
- Build `7489`
- Commit SHA `bd4fcb6`

Let me know if there's is more information I can provide to help.
